name: Levofloxacin
route_note: Once-daily oral or IV; nebulised solution (Quinsair) for cystic fibrosis in the EU; eye drops.

discovery.note: The pure levorotatory (S)-enantiomer of the racemate ofloxacin, accounting for most of its antibacterial activity.

tagline: Respiratory fluoroquinolone and key drug for drug-resistant tuberculosis
summary: Levofloxacin is the active S-enantiomer of ofloxacin, developed by Daiichi and launched in Japan in 1993. It has improved activity against Streptococcus pneumoniae and atypical pathogens and is used for pneumonia, urinary infections and drug-resistant tuberculosis, with the class warnings of all fluoroquinolones.
mechanism: Fluoroquinolones trap DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV on DNA in cleaved complexes, converting these essential enzymes into toxic agents that create double-strand DNA breaks, block replication and transcription, and trigger rapid bactericidal death. In most Gram-negative bacteria gyrase is the primary target; in many Gram-positive bacteria it is topoisomerase IV.

Compared with ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin binds pneumococcal topoisomerase IV and gyrase more effectively, giving reliable activity against S. pneumoniae while retaining moderate anti-pseudomonal activity.
uses: Community-acquired pneumonia and acute bacterial sinusitis
Complicated urinary tract infections and acute pyelonephritis
Chronic Pseudomonas infection in cystic fibrosis (inhaled, EU)

history.title: Tendon boxed warning
history.detail: The FDA adds a boxed warning on tendinitis and tendon rupture to all systemic fluoroquinolones.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic levofloxacin becomes available in the US.

history.title: Use restricted
history.detail: The FDA advises that fluoroquinolones should not be used for uncomplicated sinusitis, bronchitis or UTI when alternatives exist, and expands the boxed warning.

history.title: EU review and aortic warnings
history.detail: The EMA recommends restricting fluoroquinolones because of disabling, long-lasting side effects; the FDA warns about hypoglycaemia, mental-health effects and aortic aneurysm or dissection.

serious: Tendinitis and tendon rupture (especially with corticosteroids and in older people)
safety.boxed_warning: Fluoroquinolones are associated with disabling and potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions, including tendinitis and tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy and central nervous system effects, and may exacerbate muscle weakness in myasthenia gravis; for acute sinusitis, acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis and uncomplicated urinary tract infection, reserve for patients with no alternative treatment options.

facts: Levofloxacin's near-complete oral bioavailability means oral and IV doses are the same.
